title: Extension and Development for Participation Operations of Mangosteen Collaborative Farmers in Phato, Chumphon Province / การส่งเสริมและพัฒนาการมีส่วนร่วมในการดำเนินงานของเกษตรกรแปลงใหญ่มังคุดอำเภอพะโต๊ะ จังหวัดชุมพร
author: GITTIPHON JITJUM; กิตติพร จิตจำ; Chalermsak Toomhirun; เฉลิมศักดิ์ ตุ้มหิรัญ; Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University; Chalermsak.Too@stou.ac.th
category: การส่งเสริมและการผลิต
abstract: The objectives of this research were to study 1) general conditions and production conditions of mangosteen, 2) participation operations of mangosteen collaborative farmers, 3) problems and suggestions regarding of participation operations of mangosteen collaborative farmers, 4) comparison of the receipt and demand of participation of mangosteen collaborative farmers, and 5) guidelines for extension and developing participation operations of.This research was survey research. The population studied was mangosteen collaborative farmers in Phato District, Chumphon Province, totaling 245 persons. The sample group was determined using Taro Yamane's formula with an error of 0.05, resulting in a sample of 152 persons. Simple random sampling through a lottery system. An interview form was used to collect data and analyze the data using statistics, frequency distribution, percentage, minimum value, maximum value, mean, standard deviation, ranking, t-test, and content analysisThe research results found that 1) Farmers were male, 72.37 %, with an average age of 50.19 years old, an average of 11.51 years of mangosteen growing experience, an average mangosteen yield per rai of 1,642.76 kilograms/year, an average mangosteen production cost of 34,714.61 Baht/rai. Mangosteen orchards were mixed, with pruning, disease prevention, pest control, and weed control using chemicals. Mangosteens were harvested when the fruit was light yellow-pink, and the quality was sorted and cleaned before being sold at the group office. 2) Farmers give importance to participation in decision-making, information access, follow-up, joint thinking and planning, joint benefit sharing, and implementation at a high level. 3) Farmers have problems in decision-making and information access at a low level. Follow-up, joint benefit sharing, joint thinking and planning, and implementation at a moderate level. Suggestions for addressing low product prices include the implementation of price guarantee contracts, while addressing poor product quality can be achieved by collaborating to source only high-quality produce for sale. Additionally, establishing credibility for mangosteen quality should be pursued through public relations campaigns. 4) Farmers favored extension of participation over direct receipt in the domains of
